title: What are the most unusual RPG Maker games currently being made?

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
Well the title speaks for itself really. I've always been interested in the outlier games made on RPG maker, the outlier that made the engine do something a bit different.
I suppose one of the first unusual game to be well known was 'Yume Nikki' yes there were unusual game before that but none that really became a big name. With some of the most obvious being things like 'LISA: The Painful,' 'OneShot,' and for horror 'The Witch's House' and 'Mad Father.'
But who is working on something that looks and plays that bit different now?

Technically Laurel's Day falls into this. It's a emotional story that is disguised as a game. So you play it like a game, and find out in the end that it never was a game to begin with, but the delusions of a child going through terrible guilt.

posts.body:
Sit-Back Attack
looks to be a very well done RPG maker Idle game out within a month.

posts.author: Spiga-ize
posts.body:
The projects people work on are crazy-good! Definitely some great skills and concept design to work toward.
I don't know about "unusual", but I haven't seen a lot of maze-runner games. I'm working on one with specific biomes, biome-based enemies, and character-specific abilities. I'm about halfway through the levels. It is like a dust-bunny compared to the work others are doing.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I will make a shameless plug for my Sudoku project what I will eventually finish. I think that is probably pretty unusual for an RPG Maker game. I have a Game in Development link in my signature and I have made some YouTube videos about the development too.
But honestly, all of the projects that I'm working on and experimenting with are outside the usual JRPG-style RPG Maker games because those don't really appeal to me.
I would also put in a plug for a game that I have helped with play testing from
@PlayGG_Doctor
called Pixel Pixie and that is available on Steam. It is a very interesting concept that uses auto-battling. Something that I honestly would never have played because I don't like auto-battling. But I'm so glad I had the opportunity to play test the game. The auto-battle mechanic really work well. I would also classify Pixel Pixie as a little unusual for the "typical" RM game that I've seen.
Also, this game that is being made in MZ, which looks incredible and something that I would like to be able to do some day:
MZ - Chronicles of Vaeltaja: In Search of the Great Wanderer (in Early Access)
Buy Chronicles of Vaeltaja on Steam  Buy Chronicles of Vaeltaja on Itch.io  Chronicles of Vaeltaja is crpg in development by one man indie company Witchgrove Games. It takes you back to the golden era of pc-gaming when classics like Dungeon Master, Eye of the Beholder, Ultima and Lands of Lore...

posts.author: Garryg
posts.body:
Thanks for the replies. Those definitely sound interesting. I only recently rediscovered an old RPG maker XP game of mine that I thought was lost in a crash a while ago. So I'm just finishing it up now and then going to tidy it up a bit. But it evolved into something that barely resembles the average RPG Maker game at all now. The graphics appear to be polarising, possibly because of the stark aesthetic I was going for and possibly partly because of the overall look and style of the game. (Or maybe just because I'm bad at graphics!)
My one is called "The History of Hauntly Hall" and some older in-development stuff can be seen on this site. I think there are still some glitches in the graphics seen on here though.
It's hard to get feedback when "One of these things is not like the others"
​
